---
title: "Examples"
subtitle: "Common test cases, and a run from start to finish."
description: "Worked _quarto.tests blocks for expected failures, output checks, skips, and project defaults, with the output of a real extension-test run."
---

Each case below is a `.qmd` document under `tests/`, next to `tests/_quarto.yml`.
The `_quarto.tests` block uses the keys that q2 `quarto call test` reads.

## A case with nothing to declare

A document with no `_quarto.tests` block is a complete case.
It renders to every format `quarto inspect` reports, and passes when the log has no error and no warning.

```markdown
---
title: "Default greeting"
format:
  html: default
  typst: default
---

{{{< greeting >}}}
```

## A render that should fail

Set `shouldError` to check that the extension stops a render it should stop.
The case passes when the render exits with an error code, or when the log has an error line.
It fails with `unexpected-pass` when the render is clean.

```markdown
---
title: "Expected failure"
format: html
_quarto:
  tests:
    html:
      shouldError: true
      printsMessage:
        level: ERROR
        regex: "unknown icon"
---

{{{< boom >}}}
```

A timeout never counts as the expected failure.

## One format only

Each format key names a format to render.
A case that applies to one format names that format only.

```markdown
---
title: "Typst only"
format:
  html: default
  typst: default
_quarto:
  tests:
    run:
      extension-test:
        description: "The Typst output uses the native function."
    typst:
---
```

## Check the output

Each pattern list has two parts: the patterns that must match, and the patterns that must not match.
Set `keep-typ: true` to check the Typst source of a `typst` render.

```markdown
---
title: "Backup removed"
format:
  html: default
  typst:
    keep-typ: true
_quarto:
  tests:
    html:
      ensureFileRegexMatches:
        - ["Always here"]
        - ["Backup"]
    typst:
      ensureTypstFileRegexMatches:
        - []
        - ["Backup"]
---
```

## Expected warnings

Use `noErrors` with `printsMessage` when the extension warns on purpose.
`noErrors` allows the warnings, and `printsMessage` checks that the expected one is there.

```markdown
---
title: "Undeclared group"
format: html
_quarto:
  tests:
    html:
      noErrors: true
      printsMessage:
        level: WARN
        regex: "undeclared group"
---
```

## One document for each option value

Write one document for each value of an option that you want to test.
Each document sets the value, and has its own checks.

```markdown
---
title: "Static: all"
format:
  typst:
    keep-typ: true
extensions:
  veil:
    static: all
_quarto:
  tests:
    typst:
      ensureTypstFileRegexMatches:
        - []
        - ["Backup"]
---
```

```markdown
---
title: "Static: none"
format:
  typst:
    keep-typ: true
extensions:
  veil:
    static: none
_quarto:
  tests:
    typst:
      ensureTypstFileRegexMatches:
        - ["Backup"]
---
```

## A case to skip for now

A string in `run.skip` becomes the message of the skipped case in `results.json`, so the reason stays next to the result.

```yaml
_quarto:
  tests:
    run:
      skip: "Waits for the fix in the next Quarto release."
```

## Defaults for every case

`_quarto.tests.run.extension-test` in `tests/_quarto.yml` applies to every document, and each document overrides it key by key.
No other key under `_quarto.tests` is allowed there.

```yaml
# tests/_quarto.yml
project:
  type: extension-test

_quarto:
  tests:
    run:
      extension-test:
        timeout: 120
```

## A run from start to finish

This is the repository's `clean` fixture, an extension with one shortcode and a `_schema.yml`, and no authored test document:

```bash
quarto pandoc lua _extensions/extension-test/run.lua \
  --root tests/fixtures/clean --tests tests/fixtures/clean/_t
```

The summary goes to standard error:

```txt
  conformance  ok    5 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped
  render       skip  0 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped
  smoke        ok    4 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped
  PASS: 11 cases, 9 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped, 0 warnings
```

The TAP goes to standard output:

```txt
TAP version 13
1..11
ok 1 - conformance/manifest/clean
ok 2 - conformance/path/clean/shortcodes/clean.lua
ok 3 - conformance/schema/clean
ok 4 - conformance/descriptors/clean
ok 5 - conformance/defaults/clean
ok 6 - conformance/vendored/clean # SKIP no-dependency-manifest
ok 7 - render/discover # SKIP no-test-document
ok 8 - smoke/generated/clean-options-defaults/html
ok 9 - smoke/generated/clean-options-full/html
ok 10 - smoke/generated/clean-shortcode-clean-minimal/html
ok 11 - smoke/generated/clean-shortcode-clean-full/html
```

The render layer had nothing to render, and says so.
The smoke layer still tested the shortcode four ways from the schema alone.

## Continuous integration

This workflow tests on the release and pre-release channels every week, and on each pull request that touches the extension or its tests.
When the weekly run fails, it opens an issue, or comments on the one it opened before:

```yaml
# .github/workflows/test.yml
name: Test

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "_extensions/**"
      - "tests/**"
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 6 * * 1"

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  test:
    uses: mcanouil/quarto-extension-test/.github/workflows/extension-test.yml@main
    with:
      quarto-channels: '["release", "pre-release"]'
  issue:
    needs: test
    if: ${{ failure() && github.event_name == 'schedule' }}
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write
    uses: mcanouil/quarto-extension-test/.github/workflows/extension-test-issue.yml@main
```

A failing pull request shows up on the pull request itself, so the issue is kept for the scheduled run.
The `issues: write` permission belongs to the `issue` job alone.
Leave that job out, and the workflow needs nothing beyond `contents: read`.
